 Advertisement Updated: 6:13 PM PST Nov 17, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Jeremiah Martinez Digital Producer Shelter-in-place order lifted after reported gas leak in Stockton neighborhood
 Updated: 6:13 PM PST Nov 17, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Jeremiah Martinez Digital Producer STOCKTON, Calif. — A shelter-in-place order has been lifted after a reported gas leak in a San Joaquin County neighborhood, according to the sheriff's office. 
 The San Joaquin County Sheriff's Office said a gas leak was reported in the area of Highway 26 and White Lane, just outside of Stockton. 
 Advertisement Deputies received reports that a pipe was hit and crews are working to shut off the gas in the area, the sheriff's office said. 
 Officials said residents within a quarter-mile radius are being asked to shelter in place as a precaution and turn off all ignition sources. Residents are also being asked to not use open flames, light fires, or operate anything that could create a spark. 
 "We understand this may be concerning, but these precautions are being taken to help keep everyone safe," the sheriff's office said. "Please remain indoors and follow these safety instructions until further notice."
